question: Reference iba\app\docs\escalation-304-orphan-justification-review-v1-20260723.md Part A -- 6 orphan configs (not referenced anywhere in iba/app/**/*.py). An "orphan" here means: cfg_setting.key or cfg_enum.name does not appear as a literal string in any .py file under iba/app/, excluding migration/*.py (write-once bootstrap scripts do not count as usage). It seems that the check for usage of a config is inadequate. The check is supposed to confirm that the config is actually used in the application. Usage is defined differently for different types of config. In most cases code will use the config name in the code, to apply the value of the config in the code - so the test is if the value of the config change, will the code automatically respond to it. In other cases, such as governance.* configs must be read by the startup routine explicitly to ensure that AI complies with it; in other cases the config is a lookup, or options, which I assume is not hard coded but uses the config. Validating the use of configs is a method of ensuring that the configs are not ignored in the code, and that a change in config will change the behaviour of the code.
